item.title: Linguistic Passiveness in Earnings Calls and Stock Returns
item.description: arXiv:2610.19087v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study linguistic passiveness as the fraction of passive-voice sentences in earnings conference call Q&A sessions and show it is informative for equity markets. Using 105,642 U.S. calls from 2008 to 2024, passiveness is negatively associated with announcement-day returns among positive-surprise firms: returns fall from 4.38% to 2.74% across passiveness quintiles. This announcement-day discount fully reverses over the subsequent quarter, indicating a temporary mispricing when news is good. For negative-surprise firms, passiveness has no announcement-day effect but predicts negative long-run returns, consistent with investor under-attention when salient bad news dominates. Passiveness remains informative after controlling for sentiment and standard readability proxies, suggesting that linguistic passiveness captures a distinct yet important dimension of managerial communication.
item.dc:creator: Lynn Tao, Yuntao Wu, Charles Martineau, Vincent Gr\'egoire, Andreas Veneris

item.title: BioPRM: Step-Level Consistency Verification of Biological Protocols
item.description: arXiv:2610.19657v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Process reward models (PRMs) provide fine-grained supervision for assessing intermediate steps in language-model outputs, but their application to biological protocols presents distinct challenges. Protocol validity depends on both the appropriateness of individual operations and their consistency with the experimental objective and surrounding procedure, while experimental outcomes are typically unavailable during verification. We introduce BioPRM, a contextual process reward model for identifying procedural inconsistencies in structured biological protocols. We construct a supervision corpus from SciRecipe and protocols collected from protocols.io and Bio-protocol using LLM-assisted construction and source-specific review by personnel with biological expertise.
item.dc:creator: Bowen Shao, Ziyang Ling, Ronald Xu, Mingzhai Sun

item.title: A posteriori error bounds for cumulative energy fields in irreversible gradient damage
item.description: arXiv:2610.19794v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Cumulative energy fields in irreversible evolution depend on the loading path, even when terminal states and global work agree. We derive a posteriori bounds for these fields in scalar gradient damage with a prescribed driving density. A perturbation estimate for the incremental obstacle map yields a continuous loading history, which is enclosed by nondecreasing residual supersolutions. A primitive identity transfers this enclosure to the cumulative field. An exact endpoint-rule defect and outward arithmetic certify the output delivered by the numerical method. The analysis separates spatial, loading, and algebraic errors and gives sufficient conditions for certificate decay. Computable realizations use splines and verified supersolutions in one dimension and on two-dimensional rectangles. The production bounds cover the independently enclosed errors of all 417 saved histories from 28 adaptive calculations and all 25 fixed-parameter controls. In a narrow-localization case, the verified relative error decreases from approximately 158.78\% to below 2.125\% at a 5\% certified target. Source-oriented marking reduces accumulated matrix--vector work by 35.9\% and 51.9\% in two comparisons. A mechanically generated two-dimensional benchmark shows how auxiliary supersolutions sharpen constant barriers and enable acceptance of both loading orders.
item.dc:creator: Yubo Huang, Xiongyu Hu, Xin Lai, Cheng Lyu

item.title: Sounds Cheesy - Bridging the Texture Gap Between Dairy and Plant-Based cheese with Non-Contact Ultrasound and AI
item.description: arXiv:2610.19924v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Plant-based cheeses often fail to reproduce the texture of dairy cheese. Closing this gap is slow because the reference methods, texture profile analysis (TPA) and sensory panels, destroy the sample and are poorly suited to screening many formulations in a timely and cost-effective manner. Here we show that non-contact, air-coupled ultrasonic imaging combined with machine learning can characterise cheese texture rapidly and without damaging the sample. Thirteen commercial products (nine dairy, four plant-based; 119 slices, 357 scans) were imaged in through-transmission at 100 kHz to give two-channel amplitude and time-of-flight C-scans, and each slice was then measured by TPA. The C-scans revealed millimetre-scale acoustic domains in ripened dairy cheeses, consistent with their fused-curd microstructure, that were absent from the homogeneous starch and oil matrix of the plant-based products. TPA showed that the texture gap is one of range and failure behaviour rather than average firmness. Mean hardness was similar for the two categories, but dairy products spanned a 7.5-fold range against 1.9-fold for plant-based products, and the plant-based products failed in a brittle, strain-softening manner rather than by ductile yielding. No single ultrasonic parameter tracked texture across products. However, a compact convolutional neural network predicted full true stress-strain loading and unloading curves from the C-scan images of unseen slices across all thirteen products without product-specific calibration. Clustering the predicted curves produced a texture map on which three plant-based slices sat with the Cheddars and one with Emmental, while soft, mozzarella-like textures remained unoccupied. The approach offers a one-minute, non-contact measurement suited to formulation screening and at-line quality control of cheese.
item.dc:creator: Wenjing Feng, Thomas A. Hazlehurst, Nik Watson

item.title: Transverse impulse response of finite and infinite Rayleigh beams
item.description: arXiv:2610.19986v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Here, we study an undamped Rayleigh beam subjected to a concentrated transverse impulse applied at a point far from the boundaries. For a simply supported finite beam struck at its midpoint, using the modal expansion of the impulse response, a short-time asymptotic series for the response of the struck point is derived. The infinite beam impulse response is obtained as a spectral integral in two ways. The spectral integral is evaluated exactly in terms of modified Bessel functions via Laplace transform calculations. The corresponding short- and long-time asymptotics of the exact integral are consistent with the power series developed earlier and the Euler-Bernoulli beam, respectively. Direct numerical evaluation of the integral with a pre-specified error bound and numerical contour integration is also presented for verification. An ad hoc approximation is given which matches the response well for all times. The relationship between finite and infinite beam responses is examined in some detail. There are three consequences of finite length. First, the coefficients in the power series expansion contain components that decay exponentially with increasing length of the beam. Second, a smooth deviation from the infinite beam response is observed, consistent with the greatest group velocity in the beam, wherein a small precursor is detected which is consistent with broader theory. Third, a slope discontinuity is observed, corresponding to the high-frequency limit of group velocity. The full time series plot from modal expansion satisfactorily shows both the arrival and passage of these high frequency components. This paper opens the door to impact studies that are envisaged in future work.
item.dc:creator: Saranya Biswas, Anindya Chatterjee

item.title: Generating Accurate Microstructures of Anisotropic Magnetorheological Elastomers
item.description: arXiv:2610.20289v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Anisotropic magnetorheological elastomers are magnetoactive smart materials whose complex magneto-mechanical behavior is strongly influenced by their underlying microstructure. Efficient and accurate multiscale simulations of these materials rely on small unit cells that reproduce the behavior of the real material. In this work, we present a framework for the generation and validation of such two-dimensional representative volume elements (RVEs) from a given microstructure image, assuming circular particles. The cells are generated through an optimization procedure where the two-point correlation function serves as a differentiable descriptor, while a minimum inter-particle distance is enforced as a constraint. To assess the equivalence of the generated cells, we compare their effective magneto-mechanical response with those of the reference microstructure. We demonstrate that the generated cells reproduce the reference response with high accuracy, also with substantially fewer particles. Consequently, the computational cost of subsequent multiscale simulations is reduced.
item.dc:creator: Heinrich T. Roth, Lukas Jabs, Matti Schneider, Konstantin Gerstenberger, G\"unter K. Auernhammer, Karl A. Kalina, Markus K\"astner

item.title: BizBench: Unveiling Hidden Challenges in Deploying Long-Horizon Agents for Real-World Business
item.description: arXiv:2610.20424v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Existing long-horizon agent benchmarks often emphasize final task success while providing limited assessment of intermediate execution validity. Yet real-world business operations require agents to navigate extensive, potentially outdated or conflicting policies while satisfying critical constraints throughout execution. These requirements are particularly consequential in high-stakes domains such as payments, where intermediate violations can incur financial losses or regulatory consequences regardless of the final outcome. To bridge this evaluation gap, we introduce BizBench, a multi-turn benchmark grounded in real-world procedures from a leading payments company. Its executable environment integrates 789 knowledge documents and 601 discoverable business tools, with consistent policies, states, and tool behavior. The benchmark comprises 50 tasks involving resource constraints, temporal dependencies, prior commitments, and conflicting or outdated guidance. Each task is validated through reference execution, while deterministic checks assess both goal attainment and execution validity without prescribing a single solution path. Experiments reveal substantial limitations even among frontier models: Claude Opus 5 and GPT-6 Sol achieve strict success rates of only 64.0% and 61.3%, respectively. For Qwen3.8-27B, goal attainment reaches 42.0%, but strict success drops to 32.7%, demonstrating how outcome-based evaluation can mask invalid execution. Beyond success rates, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash averages 191.3 tool calls per run, approximately 70% more than reference executions, revealing substantial execution overhead. Overall, BizBench establishes a testbed for evaluating and advancing long-horizon agents beyond task completion, toward reliable and constraint-compliant execution in complex business environments.
item.dc:creator: Enhan Zhao, Yongqi Tong, Xuejun Yu, Hang Wang, Pan Wang, Yichao Wang, Di He, Jianshe Li, Wei Wu

item.title: Global Parameter Identification and Uncertainty Quantification of reduced-order ADM1 using Maximum Likelihood Estimation and Bayesian Inference
item.description: arXiv:2610.19098v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Anaerobic digestion (AD) models can be challenging to calibrate against real data due to limited practical identifiability, data scarcity, and model complexity. Weighted least squares objective functions and gradient-based solvers using finite differences are often used in literature, but result in suboptimal parameter estimates and large uncertainty bands. This paper identifies the parameters of a reduced-order ADM1 by comparing the frameworks of maximum likelihood estimation (MLE) and Bayesian inference (BI), and quantifies uncertainties of parameters and outputs. Multirate experimental data are taken from a lab-scale AD reactor fed with agricultural substrates and operated at organic loading rates of 3$\,$g VS $\mathrm{m^{-3}d^{-1}}$. Global optima are found via global and gradient-based local search algorithms using forward sensitivities. Enhanced scatter search provides the best global search results. These are refined by the Gauss-Newton algorithm as the best local search, which delivers $R^2$ values of 0.95 for acetic acid and 0.77 for biogas production. BI yields substantially narrower uncertainty bands than MLE and avoids the need for a global search by incorporating prior knowledge about parameter distributions. The search space is captured efficiently by log10 scaling of parameters. Algorithmic details on its implications are provided. Despite a high-resolution lab-scale dataset, the ADM1-specific inhibition parameter $K_\mathrm{I,nh3}$ is practically not identifiable with MLE, and shows a low output sensitivity, whereas a parameter for the effective ion concentration shows superb practical identifiabilty at high confidence with both MLE and BI. The present work lays a scalable base for calibration of nonlinear AD models by providing reliable simulations. It thus advances model-based monitoring and control applications of multirate processes such as agricultural AD plants.
item.dc:creator: Simon Hellmann, Leander Lerch, Terrance Wilms, Moritz Reumsch\"ussel, Alberto Meola, F\'elix Delory, Steffi Knorn, Stefan Streif, S\"oren Weinrich

item.title: Beyond Time Induction: Structured Conditional Neural Solvers for Parametric Stochastic-Volatility Pricing
item.description: arXiv:2610.19254v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Physics-informed neural networks provide a flexible framework for learning parametric PDE solution families without labeled data, yet preserving accurate derivatives across heterogeneous regimes remains challenging. Structured neural solvers offer compact representations, but restrictive conditional parameterizations can limit adaptation across the solution family. We introduce BeTINN, a structured conditional architecture extending time-induced modulation through multi-directional time-parameter conditioning and a joint residual pathway. We evaluate BeTINN on the Heston stochastic-volatility PDE, a demanding parametric problem with mixed derivatives and economically relevant first- and second-order sensitivities. BeTINN improves joint accuracy across normalized option value and key sensitivity metrics relative to our baselines. Controlled ablations characterize the roles of its architectural components. We further find that validation physics loss is informative but does not fully determine differential fidelity, and that accurate solution values can coexist with localized derivative errors. These results support structured conditional adaptation and motivate derivative-aware evaluation when sensitivities are downstream quantities of interest.
item.dc:creator: Jose Miguel Lara Rangel, Mixtli Vazquez Mendoza

item.title: Recognition Is Not Grounding: Benchmarking Multilingual Financial Evidence Extraction
item.description: arXiv:2610.19432v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Comparing financial disclosures across languages requires identifying shared accounting concepts and recovering all numerical facts that express them. Existing benchmarks evaluate aspects of these capabilities, but provide limited insight into whether both succeed on the same multilingual evidence. In particular, it remains unclear whether language models can recognize these concepts across languages and exhaustively recover their corresponding numerical evidence from the same contexts. We introduce MULTIFINGROUND, a benchmark designed to investigate this recognition-grounding gap in multilingual financial reports. Constructed from FY2025 disclosures of 90 issuers in English, French, and Greek, MULTIFINGROUND aligns independently authored reports through a shared accounting taxonomy and provides traceable fact-level annotations. The benchmark evaluates financial fact identification, concept recognition, exhaustive fact selection, and concept discrimination without candidate labels. Across 15 evaluated models, eight API and open-weight reference models achieve 97.3-99.4\% concept recognition accuracy, yet miss at least one target fact in 26.6-41.9\% of correctly recognized groups. Further analyses reveal substantial variation in concept discrimination and limited gains from the evaluated finance-specialized models. Our findings demonstrate that strong concept recognition can coexist with incomplete evidence recovery, highlighting the importance of evaluating semantic recognition and evidence completeness together.
item.dc:creator: Lingfei Qian, Yan Wang, Xueqing Peng, Polydoros Giannouris, Nadhem Zmandar, Yi Han, Yanguang Liu, V\'ictor Guti\'errez-Basulto

item.title: MolLean: A Process-Verifiable Language for Chemical Reasoning
item.description: arXiv:2610.20459v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Chemical chain-of-thought can contain hallucinated structural and property claims. We thereby introduce MolLean, a process-verifiable language that grounds chemical reasoning in an explicit molecular state. A layered Lean-based kernel checks state transitions and assertions over molecular readouts, from primitive graph edits to compound transformations. Meanwhile, a typed witness protocol separates native structural checks from externally supplied measurements. We further introduce MolLean-MCP, a stateful tool interface that exposes these transitions, checks, and readouts during generation: the model receives feedback to decide its next action, and rejected actions leave the state unchanged. MolLean supports one-pass trace execution, whole-trace refinement, and interactive reasoning through MolLean-MCP. We evaluate these three modes with direct chain-of-thought on 8,800 matched examples across 12 tasks spanning molecular generation, editing, optimization, and reactions. With Qwen3.6-27B, whole-trace refinement outperforms direct chain-of-thought on all 12 tasks. MolLean-MCP complements whole-trace refinement with stepwise verification feedback, reaching better performance in reaction tasks. Together, these results highlight an executable foundation for chemical reasoning, in which explicit chemical commitments can be checked and revised rather than remaining solely in free-form explanations.
item.dc:creator: Jiatong Li, Yatao Bian

item.title: A finite-element-inspired bipartite graph learned simulator for manufacturability assessment in large-deformation sheet forming
item.description: arXiv:2605.22845v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Explicit dynamic finite element (FE) simulations are widely used for large-deformation analysis but remain expensive for design-space exploration. In explicit FE analysis, nodal kinematics and element-level deformation measures evolve through a coupled node-element update process. An FE-inspired learned simulator can preserve this structure and learn nodal kinematics and elemental deformation on their native domains. Nodal displacement describes geometry evolution, while elemental thinning identifies local deformation and critical regions. Feeding both outputs back during rollout allows each field to inform subsequent updates of the other. This work proposes CAtt-BiGNN, a cross-attention-based bipartite graph neural network for coupled nodal-elemental learning. The bipartite graph encodes FE-guided state organisation and information flow without imposing equilibrium or constitutive constraints. Mesh nodes and elements are represented as distinct graph entities connected by directed node-element edges, enabling prediction of nodal displacement increments and elemental deformation on their native domains. An edge-aware cross-attention processor dynamically updates edge representations and weights messages using the receiving state and evolving local relations. For larger graphs, CAtt-BiUGNN uses separate nodal and elemental downsampling and upsampling to enhance long-range propagation while preserving their interaction across graph levels. The method is evaluated on dome-shaped cold-forming and corner-shaped hot-forming benchmarks. Comparisons with node-centred baselines, an FE-inspired hypergraph model, a Physics-Attention-based neural operator, a graph Transformer, and attention ablations show improved joint accuracy in nodal displacement and elemental thinning prediction during autoregressive rollout.
item.dc:creator: Yingxue Zhao, Haoran Li, Haosu Zhou, Tobias Pfaff, Nan Li

item.title: Reference-Space Reuse for Steady and Transient State-Constrained Conjugate Heat Transfer
item.description: arXiv:2606.17971v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Repeated thermal optimization must enforce local temperature limits while solving linear systems whose unknowns change as the constraints activate and release. Zero-extension transfer, which carries correction vectors from one inactive set to the next, assigns zero to the degrees of freedom that a constraint has just released. We construct a spectral reference on the full state domain before optimization and restrict it directly to the current inactive set at each update, so the coarse correction receives reference entries at every released degree of freedom. Spatial and space--time constructions cover steady and transient conjugate heat transfer with prescribed fluid velocity, and a restriction-residual identity yields alignment and deflated-convergence bounds under stated rank and spectral-separation assumptions. In the primary comparisons on body-fitted transformer and bore-in-block models, the resulting reference deflation reduces the median complete optimization time relative to the tested iterative alternatives on the same graphics processor. Complete time includes reference construction. Matched transfer experiments connect the improvement to the reference information retained at released constraints. The lower cost persists on refined Cartesian and bore-in-block meshes, on space--time trajectories and over sequences with changing loads and query order; the margin narrows, and eventually reverses, as a trajectory gains time slabs at a fixed horizon. Full-domain reference retention thus supports repeated evaluation of temperature-constrained heat inputs in engineering thermal models.
item.dc:creator: Teeratorn Kadeethum, Francesco Ballarin, Youngsoo Choi, Sanghyun Lee

item.title: Temperature-Dependent Multiphysics Modeling of Additive Friction Stir Deposition Using Multi-Task Coupled Physics-Informed Neural Networks
item.description: arXiv:2610.04082v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Additive friction stir deposition (AFSD) involves coupled thermal and material-flow fields governed by frictional heating, plastic deformation, and tool-imposed boundary conditions. High-fidelity finite-volume methods (FVMs) can resolve these fields but are computationally expensive, while constant-property approximations can distort the predicted thermo-mechanical response. This work develops a steady-state multi-task coupled physics-informed neural network (MCoPINN) to predict three-dimensional temperature and material-flow fields while reconstructing temperature-dependent thermal conductivity, density, and specific heat from sparse property measurements. A theoretical analysis decomposes prediction error into property reconstruction and neural field-solver contributions and characterizes the discrepancy associated with constant-property models. A controlled one-dimensional nonlinear-conduction study evaluates property reconstruction under sparse measurements. The framework is then evaluated for AFSD against a temperature-dependent FVM benchmark and experimental thermocouple measurements. MCoPINN reproduces the reference thermal and material-flow fields and reduces average temperature root-mean-square error from 50.13 K for the constant-property CoPINN to 30.28 K across four traverse speeds. MCoPINN requires approximately 8.5 hours of training per condition, compared with 52 hours for the FVM benchmark. These results demonstrate computationally efficient, physics-coupled prediction with temperature-dependent material properties.
item.dc:creator: Dhrubajyoti Gupta, Nikhil Gotawala, Raghav Gnanasambandam, Rohit Kannan, Jian Yu, Hang Z. Yu, Zhenyu James Kong

item.title: Fundamental Limitations of QAOA on Constrained Problems and a Route to Exponential Enhancement
item.description: arXiv:2511.17259v5 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study the feasibility limitations of generic QAOA for permutation-constrained optimization, where valid configurations occupy an exponentially small fraction of the Boolean hypercube. Using random edge-cost TSP/ATSP ensembles, we establish high-probability bounds showing that optimized generic QAOA retains exponentially small feasible probability over specified parameter domains. At depth one, the bound holds uniformly over all mixer angles and a cost-angle grid that may be exponentially large in n^2. The analysis combines Walsh-Fourier/Krawtchouk estimates, which suppress low- and high-degree contributions, with transition-feature collision bounds controlling objective-dependent interference. Complementary cost-angle averaging, fourth-moment estimates, and light-cone analysis characterize energy-fibre coherence, typical-angle concentration, and constraint-correlation geometry. We compare generic QAOA with a constraint-enhanced kernel (CE-QAOA) initialized in a product one-hot subspace and evolved with a block-local XY mixer. For N = n^2 binary variables, CE-QAOA attains feasible probability at least n!/n^n at every depth, yielding an exp[Omega(n^2)] advantage over optimized generic QAOA at depth one with high probability. For linked cost-angle schedules with independently optimized mixer angles, the generic feasibility obstruction and exponential CE-QAOA separation extend throughout linear-depth windows p <= alpha*n, for fixed alpha > 0. These parameter-uniform bounds also imply exponential raw-sample requirements for adaptive feasible sampling within the prescribed domains.
item.dc:creator: Chinonso Onah, Kristel Michielsen

item.title: Interpolation of GEDI Biomass Estimates with Calibrated Uncertainty Quantification
item.description: arXiv:2601.16834v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Wall-to-wall biomass density estimation from NASA's GEDI mission requires interpolating sparse LIDAR observations across heterogeneous landscapes. While Random Forest and XGBoost are widely used, they predict each location independently from satellite features, without adapting to the varying difficulty of heterogeneous landscapes. We introduce Attentive Neural Processes (ANPs), a probabilistic meta-learning architecture that explicitly conditions predictions on local observation sets as well as geospatial foundation model embeddings. ANPs learn a flexible spatial covariance approximator that is more uncertain in complex landscapes and less in homogeneous areas. We validate this approach across five distinct biomes ranging from tropical Amazonian forests to boreal, temperate, and alpine ecosystems, demonstrating that ANPs achieve competitive accuracy while maintaining uncertainty calibration. We demonstrate a scalable, empirically calibrated alternative to ensemble architectures for continental-scale biomass mapping.
item.dc:creator: Robin Young, Srinivasan Keshav

item.title: Ideological Bias in LLMs' Economic Causal Reasoning
item.description: arXiv:2604.21334v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Do large language models (LLMs) exhibit systematic ideological bias when reasoning about economic causal effects? As LLMs are increasingly used in policy analysis and economic reporting, where directionally correct causal judgments are essential, this question has direct practical stakes. We present a systematic evaluation by extending the EconCausal benchmark with ideology-contested cases - instances where intervention-oriented (pro-government) and market-oriented (pro-market) perspectives predict divergent causal signs. From 10,490 causal triplets (treatment-outcome pairs with empirically verified effect directions) derived from top-tier economics and finance journals, we identify 1,056 ideology-contested instances and evaluate 20 state-of-the-art LLMs on their ability to predict empirically supported causal directions. We find that ideology-contested items are consistently harder than non-contested ones, and that across 17 of 20 models, accuracy is systematically higher when the empirically verified causal sign aligns with intervention-oriented expectations than with market-oriented ones. Moreover, when models err, their incorrect predictions disproportionately lean intervention-oriented, and this directional skew is not eliminated by one-shot in-context prompting. These results highlight that LLMs are not only less accurate on ideologically contested economic questions, but systematically less reliable in one ideological direction than the other, underscoring the need for direction-aware evaluation in high-stakes economic and policy settings.
item.dc:creator: Donggyu Lee, Hyeok Yun, Jungwon Kim, Junsik Min, Sungwon Park, Sangyoon Park, Jihee Kim

item.title: Real-Time GPU-Accelerated Monte Carlo Evaluation of Safety-Critical AEB Systems Under Uncertainty
item.description: arXiv:2604.27193v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Automatic Emergency Braking (AEB) systems represent a safety-critical national interest, with the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standard (FMVSS No. 127) requiring AEB in all new light vehicles sold in the United States by September 2029. However, production implementations frequently rely on deterministic stopping-distance or Time-to-Collision (TTC) thresholds that fail to capture uncertainty in sensing, road conditions, and vehicle dynamics. This paper presents a GPU-accelerated Monte Carlo framework for stochastic evaluation of emergency braking performance using a longitudinal vehicle model incorporating aerodynamic drag, road grade, brake actuator dynamics, and weight transfer effects. A one-thread-per-sample execution strategy exploits the independence of Monte Carlo rollouts, while deterministic CPU-generated sampling ensures bit-exact numerical consistency between CPU and GPU implementations. The framework is evaluated across four hardware platforms: two laptop GPUs (GTX 1650, RTX 5070) and two automotive-grade embedded platforms (Jetson Orin Nano, Jetson AGX Orin). Peak speedups of 54.57x are achieved. Real-time feasibility analysis with a complete AEB timing budget demonstrates that the Jetson AGX Orin can execute approximately 25,000 Monte Carlo samples within a 530 ms budget, enabling real-time probabilistic AEB evaluation as part of a complete embedded pipeline. Collision probability analysis demonstrates that a threshold set at the mean stopping distance of 79.2 m leaves a collision probability of approximately 47%, while the conservative 1% risk threshold requires a minimum safe headway of 111.1 m, an additional 31.9 m (40%). These results provide quantitative guidance for risk-aware AEB threshold selection under the NHTSA final rule.
item.dc:creator: Akshay Karjol, Shadi Alawneh

item.title: STREAM: Stochastic Riemannian Flow Matching with Anisotropic Decoder for Digital Histopathology Image Generation
item.description: arXiv:2606.07036v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Synthetic histopathology image generation addresses patient-privacy concerns and the growing data demands of foundation models. Existing state-of-the-art histopathology generative models use pretrained Vision Foundation Models (VFMs) as conditioning signals. We show this yields conditioning-dominated diversity: on TCGA-BRCA, 62-75% of their output diversity is attributable to the conditioning signal rather than the learned latent space, while de novo synthesis still requires a VFM at inference. We instead use histopathology VFMs as the latent space itself: their patch tokens are $\ell_2$-normalized on the unit hypersphere $\mathcal{S}^{d-1}$ with strong angular dominance and intrinsic curvature, motivating a Riemannian formulation. We present STREAM, the first framework to apply Riemannian flow matching in the histopathology domain, in two stages: 1) a bridge-type stochastic perturbation that establishes per-token rectifiability on $\mathcal{S}^{d-1}$ for training a Diffusion Transformer, and 2) a novel decoder training design whose noise covariance is anisotropic in the left-singular basis of the per-token tangent-projected velocity-field Jacobian, spending a large robustness budget on its low-response directions and a small one on its high-response directions. Across TCGA-BRCA and TCGA-COADREAD, STREAM achieves state-of-the-art gFID and ranks first on nearly all histopathology-specific metrics as well. Code and a public gallery of generated images are available at https://chokevin8.github.io/STREAM-Patho/.
item.dc:creator: Won June Cho, Daeky Jeong, Hyeongyeol Lim, Hongjun Yoon

item.title: From Clicks to Intent: Cross-Platform Session Embeddings with LLM-Distilled Taxonomy for Financial Services Recommendations
item.description: arXiv:2606.26277v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Sequential user behavior modeling is widely adopted in industrial recommender systems; however, significant gaps remain in financial services, where pre-login web interactions and authenticated in-app experiences differ drastically. Specifically, pre-login web users typically explore new products, whereas logged-in app users focus on account servicing. Due to the challenge of cross-channel entity resolution (e.g., matching anonymous web sessions to authenticated mobile accounts), web-based intent signals remain underutilized for post-authentication personalization. Existing methods for capturing web-based intent are often ad-hoc and narrow, lacking the flexibility to support both quantitative downstream recommendations and qualitative understanding at scale. In this work, we propose a scalable and dual-purpose intent prediction framework for web-based interactions and demonstrate its applicability for personalization. Our approach transforms raw web clickstreams into two outputs: a self-supervised Transformer encodes multi-modal clickstreams into a compact session embedding, while an LLM-based taxonomy generation and distillation pipeline produces interpretable intent labels. Our system demonstrates that self-supervised clickstream representations combined with LLM-distilled taxonomies can jointly serve quantitative tasks and qualitative understanding in production: on the mobile homepage tile ranking task, the session embedding improves macro Recall@1 by 1.88% and reduces Log Loss by 13.38% over production baselines. On the user conversion prediction task, the embedding outperforms the LLM labels by 4.3% on micro F1, while the distillation layer delivers interpretable labels at ultra-low latency with only a 7% performance drop.
item.dc:creator: Dianjing Fan, Yao Li, Kyaw Hpone Myint, Dwipam Katariya, Alexandre G. R. Day, Pranab Mohanty, Giri Iyengar

item.title: Use Of Convolutional Neural Networks In Detection Of Branch Dieback Disease In Pequi Trees
item.description: arXiv:2610.15049v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: This study evaluates and compares five convolutional neural network (CNN) architectures, AlexNet, Inception, LeNet, VGG16, and MobileNet, for diagnosing branch dieback (seca-dos-ponteiros) in pequi trees (Caryocar brasiliense). This phytopathology represents a severe threat to tree development and fruit yield, causing substantial economic and ecological losses across the Brazilian Cerrado. The methodology implements computer vision techniques using deep learning frameworks to process and evaluate a field dataset expanded to 6,272 multi-scale images, captured via UAV and handheld sensors under uncontrolled illumination. The models were trained to detect pathological visual patterns across leaves, branches, and canopies. The experimental initial results reveal that architectural complexity did not guarantee diagnostic reliability, heavily parameterized networks experienced optimization failures (VGG16 collapsed into majority-class prediction), whereas compact architectures achieved greater stability. MobileNet delivered the most competitive overall performance, obtaining the highest Precision (0.71) and ROC-AUC (0.63), closely followed by LeNet (AUC = 0.62). These findings indicate the viability of lightweight CNNs as foundational tools for automated phytosanitary surveillance of native flora in resource-constrained field environments.
item.dc:creator: Ronilson Rodrigues Pinho, Elua Ramos Coutinho, Nilza de Lima Pereira Sales, Sildenir Aalves Ribeiro, Sergio Manuel Serra da Cruz
